label: Galen
summary: Greek physician of the Roman empire (129 - c. 216 AD) whose humoral system dominated European medicine for some 1,500 years.

label: Blites (Blitum)
summary: Purple amaranth, the bland pot-herb 'blite' (Greek bliton, Latin blitum) of classical and early-modern authors.

label: Beets
summary: The common beet, a Mediterranean pot-herb cultivated since antiquity; here only a point of comparison for the leaves of white blite.

label: Borage
summary: Borage, a rough-leaved blue-flowered garden herb held since the Middle Ages to comfort the heart and drive away melancholy.

label: Bugloss
summary: Garden bugloss, a bristly borage-family herb whose name (Greek 'ox-tongue') was shared by several rough-leaved cordial simples.

label: Fumitory
summary: Common fumitory, a delicate field weed reputed since antiquity to purge melancholy and clear the skin.

label: Bluebottles (Cyanus)
summary: The cornflower, 'bluebottle' of English cornfields, known to the shops as Cyanus after its deep blue colour.

label: 'disp. 15' (unidentified locus)
summary: A locus reference closing the annotator's Latin note on bugloss; the work abbreviated 'disp.' cannot be identified with confidence.
